2. The same happens through a wrapper that starts its own app-server with `codex app-server -c approval_policy="never" -c sandbox_mode="danger-full-access" --listen unix://…` and then attaches `codex --remote unix://…`. The TUI (`client_name="codex-tui"`) creates the thread itself, and the thread ends up with `approval_mode=never` but `sandbox_policy` managed/restricted — the server-side `-c sandbox_mode="danger-full-access"` is not applied. 3. Additionally (= #49088/#49865): an older thread that had been running as `DangerFullAccess` on the daemon dropped to `WorkspaceWrite` after `codex app-server daemon restart`.

`--yolo` (and `-c sandbox_mode="danger-full-access"` on the app-server) should result in `approval_mode=never` + `danger-full-access` for threads created from that TUI, regardless of whether the TUI runs in-process, on the managed daemon, or via `--remote`.

### Additional information

Workaround: put `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` and `approval_policy = "never"` in `~/.codex/config.toml` and restart the daemo
